samples.summary: The new `DOCX_ALIGNMENTS` "closed lookup" is not closed — it resolves inherited Object.prototype keys, so a hostile `style.alignment` can still put a non-token value into `<w:jc w:val>`
samples.evidence: `const align = DOCX_ALIGNMENTS[style.alignment as string] ?? 'left'` (docx-style-map.ts:141) indexes a plain object literal, so the lookup walks Object.prototype. `alignment: 'constructor'` yields the `Object` function, `'toString'`/`'valueOf'` yield functions, `'__proto__'` yields Object.prototype — all truthy and all `!== 'left'`, so line 143 interpolates their stringification (`function Object() { [native code] }`, `[object Object]`) straight into the attribute. Attacker path: any writer of the model — the content PUT API for header/footer blocks (unvalidated, see the companion finding), the slides content PUT for element text bodies, or a crafted DOCX/PPTX import — persists `alignment: 'constructor'`; it round-trips verbatim (`packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:143` writes it, `:157` reads it back; frontend `yorkie-doc-store.ts:220` likewise) and reaches this sink on export. None of the stock prototype members contain a `"`, so this is not an attribute break today — the impact is a schema-invalid `ST_Jc` value (Word repairs/refuses the file) plus the loss of the fail-closed guarantee the comment claims, which would become a real injection if anything ever polluted Object.prototype with a quote-bearing string. Same pattern at `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:79` (`ALGN[block.style.alignment] ?? 'l'`). Fix: `Object.hasOwn(DOCX_ALIGNMENTS, k) ? ... : 'left'`, a `Map`, or a null-prototype object.

samples.summary: The new API-side alignment allowlist never runs on header/footer blocks (or on slides text-body blocks), so the same value it rejects can still be persisted through the same endpoint
samples.evidence: `assertValidBlockStyle` is only reached from `assertValidBlock`, and `assertValidDocsBody` (controller.ts:249-251) walks only `body.blocks`. But `writeDocsRoot` also persists `document.header.blocks` and `document.footer.blocks` (`packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:289-303`, each child built with the same `buildBlockNode`, whose `serializeBlockStyle` writes `alignment: style.alignment` verbatim at `:143`). So `PUT /api/v1/workspaces/:ws/documents/:id/content` with `{"blocks":[],"header":{"marginFromEdge":0,"blocks":[{"id":"b1","type":"paragraph","style":{"alignment":"center\"/><w:jc w:val=\"right"},"inlines":[]}]}}` bypasses the gate entirely, and the value flows to the *same* sink via `DocxExporter.buildHeaderFooterXml` → `blockToXml` → `buildParagraphPropertiesXml`, landing in `word/header1.xml`. The identical hole exists on the slides arm: `assertValidSlidesBody`/`assertValidElement` (controller.ts:415-435) check only `id`/`type`/`frame`, so element text-body blocks carry arbitrary `style.alignment` into `ALGN[...]` in the PPTX exporter. Header/footer blocks also skip every other block check (`id`, `type`, `style`, `inlines`), so a malformed block reaches `buildBlockNode` unguarded. Exploitability of the alignment payload is currently blocked by the exporter-side lookup — but that lookup has the prototype-chain hole reported separately, and the guard reads as covering a sink it does not cover. Fix: run `assertValidBlock` over `body.header?.blocks` / `body.footer?.blocks` (and over slides element text bodies).

samples.summary: A non-string table-cell `backgroundColor` accepted by the content API reaches `toRgbHexColor`, whose `color.trim()` throws — crashing DOCX/PDF export for every user of the document
samples.evidence: `serializeCellStyle` writes `if (s.backgroundColor) attrs.backgroundColor = s.backgroundColor;` with no `typeof === 'string'` guard, unlike the inline path two functions above (`docs-tree.ts:85`). The content PUT validator never inspects cell styles (`assertValidBlock` only checks `cells[].blocks`), so `{"tableData":{"rows":[{"cells":[{"style":{"backgroundColor":123},"blocks":[]}]}],"columnWidths":[1]}}` persists a non-string, `parseCellStyle` (`:208`) hands it back, and the new `toDocxHexColor(cell.style.backgroundColor)` (`packages/docs/src/export/docx-exporter.ts:319`) calls `color.trim()` on it (`packages/docs/src/model/color.ts:104`) → `TypeError`, aborting the export for anyone who opens/exports that doc. The pre-change `.replace('#','')` had the same fault, so this is not a regression, but the new shared normalizer is the right place to make it total (`typeof color !== 'string'` → `undefined`). Impact: denial of export, not disclosure.

samples.summary: The design doc states every `<a:srgbClr val>` is normalized by `toRgbHexColor`, but only the PPTX text path was changed — shape fills, gradients, effects and the theme part still write whatever string the model holds (escaped, so not injectable, but unnormalized)
samples.evidence: Only `storedColorToThemeColor` in `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:183-200` routes through `toRgbHexColor`. The other producers of the same attribute — `fillXml`/`solidFillXml`/`gradFillXml` (`packages/slides/src/export/pptx/color.ts:36,40,53`), `effects.ts:22`, and `theme.ts:83-84` — reach `colorChildXml`, which only does `escapeXmlAttr(c.value.replace(/^#/,'').toUpperCase())`. Element fills and theme colors are attacker-writable through the slides content PUT (which validates only `id`/`type`/`frame` per element and does not inspect `themes` entries at all) and through PPTX import, so a value like `rgb(255,0,0)` or `a"/><a:alpha val="0` still lands in the attribute as `val="a"/>..."`. Escaping keeps this out of injection territory — hence minor — but the documented invariant "the normalizer returns only [0-9A-F]{6}, which makes the attribute injection-proof by construction" (slides-pptx-export.md) and the equivalent table in docs-docx-import-export.md overstate what the code enforces. Searched: grep for `srgbClr val=`/`colorChildXml` across packages/slides/src, read color.ts, theme.ts, effects.ts, text.ts.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. The alignment allowlist (BLOCK_ALIGNMENTS, docs-content.controller.ts:254; assertValidBlockStyle :266-279) is reached only via assertValidBlock, called only from assertValidDocsBody over body.blocks (:249-251) and recursively for table-cell blocks (:322). A grep for 'header|footer' in the entire controller returns zero matches, so body.header/body.footer are never validated — yet writeDocsRoot persists them: buildTreeChildren maps document.header.blocks and document.footer.blocks through buildBlockNode (docs-tree.ts:289-303, :235-269), whose serializeBlockStyle writes `alignment: style.alignment` verbatim (:143). The very payload the spec asserts is rejected for blocks[0] (docs-content.controller.spec.ts:494) is therefore accepted at header.blocks[0] on the same PUT endpoint, and header/footer blocks additionally skip the id/type/style/inlines shape checks. The slides arm is likewise uncovered: assertValidElement (:415-435) checks only id/type/frame, and nothing walks element text-body blocks whose style.alignment reaches packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:79. I searched for counterexamples and found none: the only alignment check in packages/backend/src is the one above; writeDocsRoot (docs-tree.ts:517-538) applies no normalization before buildTreeChildren (normalizeBlockStyle lives only in packages/docs frontend model/store and in the read-back parseBlockStyle); and the global ValidationPipe (main.ts:65-72) is inert because putContent takes `@Body() body: unknown` with no DTO class. The value is currently clamped at both export sinks (docx-style-map.ts:141, pptx/text.ts:79), so this is not a live injection — but that is precisely a 'clear security weakness that isn't yet a full exploit' (major): a validation gate that reads as covering a sink it does not cover, with an unguarded parallel entry path through the same endpoint.

mergedFrom.summary: New `isEmptyStoredColor` dereferences a null `StoredColor`, crashing the render path on attacker-controlled slide JSON (stored DoS)

finding.summary: New `isEmptyStoredColor` dereferences an untrusted `StoredColor` without a type guard — a `null` color or an `{ kind: 'srgb', value: <non-string> }` persisted through the content PUT API throws a TypeError inside the paint path, crashing the renderer for every viewer of the document (stored DoS).
finding.evidence: `isEmptyStoredColor` (packages/docs/src/model/color.ts:59-63) does `if (c === undefined) return false;` then `typeof c === 'string' ? ... : c.kind === 'srgb' && c.value.trim() === ''`. For `c === null` (typeof 'object', not undefined) it evaluates `c.kind` → `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null`. For `{ kind: 'srgb', value: 42 }` it evaluates `(42).trim()` → `TypeError: c.value.trim is not a function`. Before this delta the same input was harmless: `resolve(c === '' ? undefined : c)` passed `null` straight to the resolver, and slides' `makeColorResolver` (packages/slides/src/view/canvas/text-renderer.ts:55) returns the theme text color for `c == null`, while `resolveColor` (packages/slides/src/model/theme.ts:102) returns a non-string `value` verbatim without throwing. Attack path: an authenticated caller (workspace member or API key) PUTs a slides body to `PUT /api/v1/workspaces/:ws/documents/:id/content`; `assertValidSlidesBody`/`assertValidElement` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:415-435) validate only `id`/`type`/`frame`, and `writeSlidesRoot` assigns `root.slides = document.slides` verbatim (packages/backend/src/yorkie/slides-tree.ts:104), so `slides[i].elements[j].text.blocks[k].inlines[l].style.color = null` (or `{kind:'srgb',value:42}`) is persisted unchanged. Every client that renders the deck reaches `resolveStoredColor` from `paintLayout` (packages/docs/src/view/paint-layout.ts:388, 453, 555), `table-renderer.ts:464/573` and `resolveColorAtPosition` (color.ts:182) and throws, so the canvas render loop dies for all collaborators until the poisoned value is removed out-of-band. Fix: make the guard total (`typeof c !== 'object' || c === null` → false; `typeof c.value === 'string' && c.value.trim() === ''`).

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo: isEmptyStoredColor (packages/docs/src/model/color.ts:59-63) guards only `c === undefined`, then dereferences `c.kind` and calls `c.value.trim()`, so a persisted `null` color (typeof 'object') or a non-string `value` throws a TypeError. Reachability is real end-to-end: the authenticated content PUT (docs-content.controller.ts:120, guards at :68) validates slide elements only for id/type/frame (assertValidElement:415-435) and writes the body verbatim (slides-tree.ts:104 `root.slides = document.slides`); read-time migration does not touch text inline styles (migrate.ts:156 returns non-shape elements unchanged, and only shape fill/stroke go through wrapColor:170), and no inline-color normalization exists in packages/docs/src/model. The poisoned value then hits the paint loop at paint-layout.ts:388/453/555, table-renderer.ts:464/573 and color.ts:182/187. Slides' resolver would have tolerated null (text-renderer.ts:55 `if (c == null)`), but the new guard throws before the resolver runs, so that tolerance does not protect it. Sibling helpers in the same file use total null checks (color.ts:15, :142), confirming the narrow check is an omission rather than an enforced contract. No not-present / already-guarded / counterexample ground applies; unvalidated stored input that crashes every viewer's renderer is within the security lens's unsafe-input-handling lane.

finding.summary: PPTX `<a:pPr lvl>` still raw-interpolates untrusted `block.listLevel` in the same function whose color children were just hardened
finding.evidence: `const lvl = block.listLevel ? ` lvl="${block.listLevel}"` : '';` interpolates the model value with no numeric coercion or closed lookup, into `<a:pPr algn="${algn}"${lvl}...>` (line 114). Unlike docs blocks (whose Yorkie Tree attributes are re-read with `Number(attrs.listLevel)` — frontend yorkie-doc-store.ts:459, backend docs-tree.ts:414), slides text bodies are plain JSON persisted verbatim by `writeSlidesRoot` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/slides-tree.ts:104) with no per-block validation in `assertValidElement` (docs-content.controller.ts:415-435). Vector: PUT slides content with `data.blocks[0].listLevel = '0"><a:buNone/><a:pPr algn="l'`; a victim exporting the deck gets attacker-chosen OOXML written into `ppt/slides/slideN.xml`. Same defect class as the `<w:jc>` case this change fixed; `<a:alpha val="${c.alpha}"/>` and the lumMod/tint/shade siblings in packages/slides/src/export/pptx/color.ts:25-29 interpolate model values raw for the same reason.

verdict.reason: Verified the exact code: text.ts:80 builds ` lvl="${block.listLevel}"` with no numeric coercion and no escapeXmlAttr, and text.ts:114 splices it into `<a:pPr algn="...">`, so a value containing a double quote breaks out of the attribute and injects arbitrary OOXML into ppt/slides/slideN.xml. Every other string attribute in the same file is escaped (text.ts:148, :300, :310) and xml.ts:5-18 provides the escaper, so the omission is genuine. No upstream guard: slides bodies are persisted as plain JSON verbatim (slides-tree.ts:101-108) and the REST PUT validator only checks element id/type/frame, never descending into data.blocks (docs-content.controller.ts:415-435); slides migrate.ts:121-168 does not touch text-body blocks; the docs-only Number() coercion at frontend yorkie-doc-store.ts:459 does not apply to slides. Export consumes the stored deck unfiltered (cli/src/commands/slides.ts:208). The sibling claim is also true: color.ts:25-29 interpolates lumMod/lumOff/tint/shade/alpha raw while the adjacent hex value on :35 is escaped. This is unsafe input handling / markup injection into a file a victim downloads — in the security lane and blocking at major.

mergedFrom.summary: DOCX attribute injection via `style.alignment`: the sibling sink in the very function this change hardened is still interpolated raw into `<w:jc w:val="..."/>`

finding.summary: `style.alignment` is interpolated unescaped and unvalidated into `<w:jc w:val="…">` — the same OOXML attribute-injection sink class this change hardens for colors, three lines below the fixed code
finding.evidence: buildParagraphPropertiesXml does `const align = style.alignment === 'justify' ? 'both' : style.alignment;` then `parts.push(`<w:jc w:val="${align}"/>`)` for anything that is not the literal 'left' (docx-style-map.ts:123-126). Unlike `fontFamily` (escaped at line 70-71) and now `color`/`backgroundColor` (normalized at 95/99), `align` gets neither escaping nor an allowlist. BlockStyle.alignment is typed as a closed union, but the runtime value comes from the Yorkie tree attributes with an unchecked cast: `partial.alignment = attrs.alignment as BlockStyle['alignment']` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:220), and `normalizeBlockStyle` only spreads defaults (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:272-274) — no validation anywhere on that path. Attack: a collaborator with write access to a shared doc (or anything writing the tree attr, incl. the backend docs-tree serializer) sets the block attribute `alignment` to `center"/><w:pStyle w:val="x` (or `a" w:x="`); when any other user exports the document, DocxExporter emits that string verbatim into word/document.xml (and header1.xml/footer1.xml via buildHeaderFooterXml), closing the `<w:jc>` element and injecting attacker-chosen OOXML into a file other users open in Word. Note the PPTX exporter does allowlist the same field (`ALGN[block.style.alignment] ?? 'l'`, packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:79), which is the pattern missing here. Confidence is medium only because I could not confirm the Yorkie server accepts an arbitrary `alignment` attribute value from a peer client; the exporter-side sink itself is unambiguous.

verdict.reason: The finding claims buildParagraphPropertiesXml interpolates style.alignment unescaped/unvalidated into <w:jc w:val="...">, quoting `const align = style.alignment === 'justify' ? 'both' : style.alignment;`. That code is not in the repository. docx-style-map.ts:115-120 defines a closed allowlist DOCX_ALIGNMENTS {left,center,right,justify->both}, and line 141 resolves via `DOCX_ALIGNMENTS[style.alignment as string] ?? 'left'` — the exact `ALGN[...] ?? 'l'` pattern the reviewer said was missing. Line 143 emits `<w:jc w:val="${align}"/>` only when align !== 'left', and align can only be one of the four literal map values, so a hostile attribute like `center"/><w:pStyle w:val="x` falls back to 'left' and the element is suppressed; nothing attacker-controlled reaches document.xml/header1.xml/footer1.xml. Grep for `alignment|w:jc` across packages/docs/src/**/export/*.ts confirms line 143 is the only <w:jc> sink (other hits are PDF-painter comments). Prototype-key edges (e.g. 'constructor', 'toString') yield built-in strings with no double-quote characters, so they cannot break out of the attribute either. Because the sink is already allowlisted at the exact cited lines, the upstream unchecked cast in yorkie-doc-store.ts is not exploitable through this path.

searchedFor: grep 'ALIGNMENTS|isAlignment|alignment ===|validAlign' across all packages/**/src (only layout.ts, the toolbar, and the docx export ternary match — no validator)
read normalizeBlockStyle (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:272) — plain spread, no validation
grep 'w:fill=|w:color=|w:val="${|srgbClr val=' across **/src/**/*.ts to enumerate every OOXML attribute sink
finding.summary: The docs content PUT API validates only the *shape* of `style`, not its values, so arbitrary strings persist into the CRDT and reach unescaped OOXML attribute sinks
finding.evidence:
`assertValidBlock` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:254-306) checks `id`, `type`, that `style` is an object, and array-ness of `inlines`/`tableData.rows`/`cells` — deliberately, per its own comment, "just the fields the writer unconditionally dereferences". No block-style or inline-style value is validated. `writeDocsRoot` then persists them verbatim (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:143, 174-184).

This is the enabling half of the `w:jc` injection above and is the reason that fixing only the color sinks leaves the class open: every current and future string-valued style field that an exporter interpolates is attacker-controlled. Surveyed the whole DOCX/PPTX attribute surface for other reachable string sinks — `fontFamily` is escaped (docx-style-map.ts:70-73, pptx text.ts:300), `headingLevel` is coerced with `Number()` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:438, docs-tree.ts:409) so at worst yields `Heading NaN`, `verticalAlign`/`borderStyle` are cast unchecked (yorkie-doc-store.ts:251,257) but the DOCX table writer emits no `vAlign`/`tcBorders` (docx-exporter.ts:301-323), `image.src` never enters XML (only the zip + an internally generated rId), and DOCX emits no hyperlinks at all — so `alignment` is the one live string sink today. Validating style values at the trust boundary (or per-sink allowlists) would make that robust rather than incidental.

verdict.reason: The claim that the docs PUT API validates only shape and never style *values* is false in this tree. `assertValidBlockStyle` (docs-content.controller.ts:254-279) enforces a `BLOCK_ALIGNMENTS` allowlist ('left','center','right','justify') and is called unconditionally from `assertValidBlock` (:295), including recursively for table-cell blocks (:322); controller.spec.ts:484-499 asserts the exact `'center"/><w:jc w:val="right'` payload gets a 400. The finding's cited range (assertValidBlock at 254-306) does not match the tree (281-334), indicating it describes a pre-fix revision. Independently, the sink is also closed: docx-style-map.ts:115-143 resolves alignment through the closed `DOCX_ALIGNMENTS` map with `?? 'left'`, so `<w:jc w:val>` can only ever hold an ST_Jc token — and header/footer paragraphs use the same `buildParagraphPropertiesXml` (docx-exporter.ts:186, 362-367), so no body-shape bypass reaches an unescaped attribute. Other string sinks are likewise guarded: fontFamily via escapeXmlAttr (docx-style-map.ts:70-73) and colors via toDocxHexColor which drops non-ST_HexColor values (:47-49, 95-101). The residual ask — validate all present and future style fields at the boundary — is hardening, not a live vulnerability.
